title: Why one odour drives two-thirds of the Kenyon cells, and the smallest change to the model that makes the code sparse
preregistration: Written before any run of this file. Development odours only: the held-out odours of plasticity-v2-v783.json are never presented here. The census needs no simulation. The grid, the target band and the selection rule are fixed here; the selected representation is frozen before any learning run, and nothing in this file may be changed after its first run.

odours.note: The development pair of plasticity-v783.json: three glomeruli's ORNs each, both sides.

apl_gain.form: every APL -> KC synaptic weight multiplied by the gain
apl_gain.basis: Kenyon cells excite the GABAergic APL neuron and APL inhibits them; blocking that loop makes KC odour responses denser and more correlated and stops flies learning to tell similar odours apart (Lin et al. 2014, Nat Neurosci 17:559-568, doi:10.1038/nn.3660). Shiu et al.'s model gives every synapse the same weight per synapse, so the strength of this inhibition is not constrained by the connectome; the gain is ours.

kc_threshold.form: every synaptic weight onto a KC multiplied by 1/k. Because the model's reset potential equals its resting potential (both -52 mV) and the membrane equations are linear in their input, this is exactly a KC spike threshold k times further above rest (7k mV instead of 7 mV), with every other neuron unchanged
kc_threshold.basis: Kenyon cells need coincident input on several of their claws to fire (Gruntman & Turner 2013, Nat Neurosci 16:1821-1829, doi:10.1038/nn.3547), which Shiu et al.'s shared threshold does not represent; the factor is ours.

kc_kc.form: KC -> KC synaptic weights multiplied by the value (0 mutes them)
kc_kc.basis: KCs make many synapses onto one another in the lobes; they are cholinergic and so excitatory in this model. Muting them asks how much of the dense code is recurrent. Diagnostic only: never selected.

grid: every apl_gain x every kc_threshold with kc_kc = 1; plus kc_kc = 0 at (apl_gain 1, kc_threshold 1) and at the selected point
measures: KCs firing at least one spike per trial, as a fraction of all KCs (coding level), per odour
Jaccard overlap of the KC sets of A and B (first trial of each)
spikes of the PAM-innervated MBON readout of plasticity-v783.json per trial
PAM dopaminergic neuron spikes per trial on these unrewarded odour trials
APL spikes, all spikes, and wall time

target.basis: Honegger, Campbell & Turner 2011 (J Neurosci 31:11772-11785, doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.1099-11.2011): an odour evokes responses in about 5% of KCs in an imaging plane, no odour's mean proportion exceeded 0.1, and single flies reached 0.17. The upper bound is that largest reported value; the lower bound (2%) is ours, to exclude near-silence. Our odours are abstract three-glomerulus inputs, not the paper's odours.

selection: Among the grid points (kc_kc = 1) where both development odours give a mean coding level in the target band, each odour drives at least 1% of KCs, and the readout MBONs fire at least 20 spikes per trial to each odour, choose the one with the smallest log(apl_gain) + log(kc_threshold); ties go to the smaller kc_threshold. If none qualifies, the result says so and no sparse representation is selected.
